To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the glycoproteins of hepatocellular cancer are different from those of other cancers and that their detection in blood is useful for diagnosis.

Ricinus communis lectin agglutinins II-reactive glyco-proteins were isolated from the ascites fluid of hepatocellular carcinomas and that the levels of these glycoprotein were increased in the sera of patients with hepat-ocellular carcinoma.

Ricinus communis Agglutinin II (RCAII)-reactive glycoprotein in the ascites of hepatocellular carcinomas patients were prepared by lectin affinity chromatograpy and the serum level of this glycoprotein was assessed by an ELISA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of cancer-associated glycoprotein from ascites and its use in enzyme-linked immunoabsorbent assay for hepatocellular carcinoma.
the study of the glycoprotein in the ascites of hepatocellular cancer.
the development of an enzyme-linked immunosorbit assay (ELISA) for the detection of hepatocellular cancer-associated antigens in human serum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the serum levels of these glycoprotein antigens are increased in patients with hepatocarcinoma, and they are useful as tumor markers.
the Ricinus communis lectin agglutinin reactive glycoproteins are not specific for hepatocellular carcinoma but are elevated in the serum of patients with hepatomas.

the results of the present investigation indicate that some of Ricin communis agglutin II-reactive glyco-proteins in the ascites of HCC patients may be tumor associated and that their serum level are increased in HCC patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have succeeded in the isolation of a cancer-associated glycoprotein in hepatocellular carcinomas.
Ricinus communis II-reactive glyco-proteins in hepatocellar carcinoma patients may be useful as tumor marker for hepatocellular carcinoma.
Ricinus communis lectin affinity chromatographic method is a good way to isolate cancer-associated glycoprotein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a single, high-affinity antibody to a protein of interest is a powerful approach to purify the protein from complex mixtures.
we have identified a set of glycan biomarkers for the detection of hepatocellular cancer, which is a leading cause of death worldwide.
we have developed a novel method for the synthesis of a new class of glycoprotein mimetics that can be used to study glycoprotein function and to design glycoproteins with novel functions.
